questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used.

What is the function of nucleoli?

options.B: formation of centromeres
options.C: formation of ribosomes
options.D: formation of the spindle during nuclear division

questions.questionText: What occurs when sucrose is broken down to monosaccharides?

options.A: condensation of reducing sugars releasing water
options.B: condensation of reducing sugars using water
options.C: hydrolysis, releasing reducing sugars and releasing water
options.D: hydrolysis, releasing reducing sugars and using water

questions.questionText: One naturally occurring polysaccharide is an unbranched chain of the molecule acetylglucosamine linked by β-1, 4 glycosidic bonds. There are –CH OH groups that alternate on each side of the polysaccharide chain. Many hydrogen bonds form between these unbranched chains. Which polysaccharide has a structure similar to that described?

options.B: amylopectin
options.C: cellulose
options.D: glycogen

questions.questionText: Which molecules have properties that are dependent on hydrogen bonds?

Features of four proteins, W, X, Y and Z, are described below. W consists of two polypeptides held together by disulfide bonds X consists of three polypeptides tightly coiled together Y consists of four polypeptides each with a prosthetic group Z consists of four polypeptides held together by disulfide bonds Which row correctly identifies the named proteins? antibody collagen haemoglobin

options.B: W Y X
options.C: Z X Y
options.D: Z Y X

questions.questionText: Why may fish living in ponds survive temperatures below 0°C in winter?

options.A: Fish body tissues produce an enzyme which prevents blood from freezing.
options.B: The ice on the pond surface insulates the water in the pond.
options.C: The plants in the pond help to keep the water temperature above 0°C.
options.D: The rocks in the pond warm up during the day and heat the water.

questions.questionText: Four students, 1, 2, 3 and 4, counted the number of bubbles of oxygen given off in a minute when investigating the effect of catalase from plant tissue on hydrogen peroxide. Each student repeated the experiment five times and calculated the mean number of bubbles per minute. Which have correctly calculated the mean? mean/number of student raw data/number of bubbles minute–1 bubbles minute-1

The diagram shows a metabolic pathway. enzyme 1 enzyme 2 enzyme 3 reactant substance X substance Y end product What would be the effect of adding a small amount of a non-competitive inhibitor of enzyme 2?

options.B: Substance X would increase in concentration.
options.C: Substance Y would no longer be formed.
options.D: The initial reactant would no longer be metabolised.

questions.questionText: Which of the following can increase the fluidity of the cell surface membrane at low temperatures?
Which process allows the movement of molecules that are too large to enter through a cell surface membrane?

options.B: endocytosis
options.C: exocytosis
options.D: facilitated diffusion

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the water potential of three cells. cell X –700kPa –800kPa –1000kPa In which directions will there be net movement of water by osmosis to or from cell X?
Which statement describes a cell belonging to a haploid organism that is capable of reproduction?

options.A: It has chromosomes that contain one polynucleotide chain.
options.B: It is capable of carrying out a reduction division to form gametes.
options.C: It possesses two copies of each gene as a result of fertilisation.
options.D: It will undergo cell division by mitosis during asexual reproduction.

questions.questionText: Some chemicals, used to stop tumour growth, work by preventing the DNA double helix from uncoiling and separating. During which stage of the cell cycle would they act?

options.B: interphase
options.C: metaphase
options.D: prophase

questions.questionText: Nocodazole is a chemical used in the study of mitosis. It causes all mitotic cells to stop dividing at metaphase. Which statements correctly identify how this chemical might work?
What is the maximum number of hydrogen bonds in a length of DNA containing 700 base pairs?
Which type of molecule is always the end product of transcription?

options.B: functional protein
options.C: mRNA
options.D: polypeptide

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a xerophytic leaf in different conditions, P and Q. X X P Q Which statements about the cells in layer X of the leaf in each of the conditions P and Q are correct?
The loading of sucrose into companion cells involves a number of processes listed below. Which is an active process?

options.A: the movement of H+ ions from companion cells
options.B: the movement of H+ ions into companion cells
options.C: the movement of sucrose from companion cells
options.D: the movement of sucrose into companion cells

questions.questionText: Which statement concerning transpiration is correct?

options.A: On a humid day, the water potential gradient between the intercellular air space and the external atmosphere increases to stimulate water loss by evaporation.
options.B: Water arriving at the spongy mesophyll cells via the symplast pathway must move by osmosis through the cell surface membrane before evaporation from the surface of the cells.
options.C: Water diffuses down the water potential gradient from the saturated air space through the guard cells before evaporating from the surface of the cells into the atmosphere.
options.D: Water moves up the xylem in the apoplast pathway and can continue on this pathway by osmosis to reach the spongy mesophyll cells before evaporating into the intercellular air space.

questions.questionText: Halophytes are plants that can survive in regions where they are regularly exposed to sea water. Sea water has a water potential of approximately –2500kPa. What adaptations would you expect halophytes to show?
Which features enable the aorta to withstand ventricular systole?

options.B: collagen fibres and smooth muscle
options.C: elastin fibres and endothelium
options.D: endothelium and smooth muscle

questions.questionText: Haemoglobin can bind to carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and oxygen. Which statement about the binding sites of haemoglobin is correct?

options.A: Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide bind to one site, oxygen binds to a different site.
options.B: Carbon dioxide and oxygen bind to one site, carbon monoxide binds to a different site.
options.C: Carbon monoxide and oxygen bind to one site, carbon dioxide binds to a different site.
options.D: Carbon monoxide, oxygen and carbon dioxide all bind to different sites.

options.A: B C D key pressure / kPa left ventricle aorta left atrium 0 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.8 time / s

questions.questionText: Which substances will displace oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin?
Which statement about chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is not correct?

options.A: The disease can often be reversed by treatment.
options.B: The patient coughs a lot, bringing up mucus.
options.C: The patients are normally over 30 years old.
options.D: The patient’s symptoms normally do not change.

questions.questionText: Which statement about coronary by-pass surgery is correct?

options.A: It is carried out to reduce the effects of atherosclerosis, improving the delivery of oxygen and dissolved glucose to the cardiac muscle of the heart.
options.B: It is the surgical removal of one or more coronary arteries to reduce the strain on the heart of a person with coronary heart disease.
options.C: Surgeons are able to divert blood around the diseased sections of the coronary arteries so that more oxygenated blood can be pumped round the systemic circulation.
options.D: The diseased parts of the aorta are replaced by using a section of a main artery from elsewhere in the body of the same person, to avoid rejection.

questions.questionText: How does smoking increase the risk of developing atherosclerosis?

options.B: by decreasing blood pressure
options.C: by increasing the risk of blood clotting
options.D: by reducing the oxygen supply to cardiac muscle

questions.questionText: Which development in vaccine production would be most important in the fight to eradicate measles in developing countries?

options.A: a combined vaccine to combat it and other diseases
options.B: a single vaccine, without the need for boosters
options.C: a vaccine containing only live measles viruses
options.D: a vaccine produced by genetic engineering techniques

questions.questionText: What could cause an outbreak of malaria in a country where it had been eliminated?

Termites are insects that build large nests that contain millions of termites of the same species. These nests are common in tropical savanna, which typically consists of grasses with widely spaced trees. Here, the termites feed on wood and other dead plant material. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The termites in the nest form a community, the savanna is the ecosystem and they feed as decomposers.
options.B: The termites in the nest form a community, the savanna is the ecosystem and they feed as primary consumers.
options.C: The termites in the nest form a population, the savanna is both the ecosystem and the habitat and they feed as primary consumers.
options.D: The termites in the nest form a population, the savanna is their habitat and they feed as decomposers.

options.B: aerobic anaerobic aerobic

options.D: anaerobic aerobic anaerobic
